You can drop them straight into `new maplibregl.Map({style: …})` and you’ll see a map instantly. --- ## 2. Minimal MapLibre code that works with any of the URLs above ```html MapLibre test – no API key
``` **What changed compared to your old Mapbox code** | Old Mapbox code | New MapLibre code | |-----------------|-------------------| | `import mapboxgl from 'mapbox-gl'` | `import * as maplibregl from 'maplibre-gl'` | | `mapboxgl.accessToken = 'pk.xxx'` | **Removed** – no token needed | | `style: 'mapbox://styles/mapbox/streets-v12'` | `style: ''` | | `new mapboxgl.Map(...)` | `new maplibregl.Map(...)` | | CSS class prefixes (`mapboxgl-…`) | If you style controls yourself, rename to `maplibregl-…` (most built-in controls work unchanged) | --- ## 3. If you want to keep *your own* Mapbox-style JSON 1. **Export the style** from Mapbox Studio (or copy the JSON you already have). 2. **Replace every `source` that uses `mapbox://`** with a URL that points to a free vector tile service. Either: - Use the sprite that ships with the free style you chose (e.g. OpenFreeMap already includes a sprite URL in its style JSON), **or** - Host your own sprite sheet (PNG + JSON) and point to it with `"sprite": "https://my-host.com/sprite"`. 5. Save the edited JSON (e.g. `my-style.json`) and serve it from a static location you control (GitHub Pages, Netlify, your own server, or even a local dev server). Then point MapLibre at that file: ```js style: 'https://mydomain.com/my-style.json' ``` --- ## 4. Quick sanity-check checklist | ✅ | What to verify | |---|----------------| | **Package** | `npm uninstall mapbox-gl && npm install maplibre-gl` (or just use the CDN as shown) | | **Import** | `import * as maplibregl from 'maplibre-gl'` (or the module CDN) | | **Namespace** | All `mapboxgl` → `maplibregl` (including controls, markers, etc.) | | **Token** | `mapboxgl.accessToken` line removed | | **Style URL** | Not `mapbox://…` – use one of the free URLs or a self-hosted JSON | | **Sprites / Glyphs** | Either use the ones bundled in the free style or host your own | | **Controls CSS** | If you wrote custom CSS, rename `.mapboxgl-…` → `.maplibregl-…` | | **Network** | Open DevTools → Network → confirm the style JSON loads (200) and the tile URLs are `https://…` (no 401/403) | | **Map loads** | You see the basemap, can pan/zoom, and any custom layers you added appear | If the map still shows a blank gray canvas, open the browser console: - **`Failed to load style`** → double-check the style URL is reachable and returns valid JSON. - **`Error: Source ... is not a valid source`** → you probably still have a `mapbox://` source inside the JSON. Search the file for `mapbox://` and replace it. - **CORS errors** → make sure the tile server sends `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` (most public services do). prompt: I was using Mapbox GL JS v2 in my app, including map.setFog() and some v2-specific camera features. After migrating to MapLibre, these are broken. Did I do something wrong in the migration?
[groq-gpt-oss] evals/prompts/lib/skill-p:
## TL;DR * **You didn’t miss a step – the APIs you were using simply don’t exist in MapLibre.** * `map.setFog()` → **`map.setSky()`** (the style spec’s `sky` object). * “Free-camera” helpers (`map.getFreeCameraOptions()`, `map.setFreeCameraOptions()`) → **`map.calculateCameraOptionsFromCameraLngLatAltRotation(...)`** (or the older `calculateCameraOptionsFromTo`) **+ `jumpTo` / `easeTo` / `flyTo`**. Everything else (imports, namespace, token, style URL, plugins, etc.) should already be in place if you followed the migration guide. Below is a complete “what to check / fix” checklist, plus concrete code snippets that will get your map working again. --- ## 1. Verify the Core Migration Steps | ✅ | Item | What to look for | |---|------|------------------| | 1 | **Package** | `npm uninstall mapbox-gl && npm install maplibre-gl` (or `yarn add maplibre-gl`). | | 2 | **Imports / CSS** | ```js\nimport * as maplibregl from 'maplibre-gl';\nimport 'maplibre-gl/dist/maplibre-gl.css';\n```
For CDN: use the ES-module bundle (`maplibre-gl.mjs`). | | 3 | **Namespace** | All `mapboxgl` → `maplibregl`. Also rename CSS classes (`mapboxgl-` → `maplibregl-`). | | 4 | **Access token** | Remove any `mapboxgl.accessToken = …`. | | 5 | **Style URL** | Must be a non-Mapbox URL (e.g. `https://tiles.openfreemap.org/styles/liberty` or a self-hosted style JSON). | | 6 | **Plugins** | Replace Mapbox-only plugins with MapLibre equivalents or open-source forks. | | 7 | **Mapbox REST APIs** | Swap Geocoding/Directions/etc. for Nominatim, OSRM, OpenRouteService, MapTiler, etc. | | 8 | **v2-only APIs** | **This is where you are stuck** – see the next sections. | If any of the above is still using the old Mapbox name or token, fix it first. Once the map loads (no “Failed to load style” errors), you can focus on the v2-specific features. --- ## 2. `map.setFog()` → `map.setSky()` ### Why it changed * Mapbox introduced a **`fog`** object in the style spec (v2). * MapLibre never added `fog`; instead it added a **`sky`** object that can render both a sky gradient **and** fog-like atmospheric effects. ### How to translate | Mapbox (`setFog`) | MapLibre (`setSky`) | |-------------------|---------------------| | `map.setFog({ "color": "#f8f4f0", "high-color": "#ffffff", "space-color": "#d8f2ff", "horizon-blend": 0.3 })` | ```js\nmap.setSky({\n 'sky-color': '#d8f2ff', // space-color → sky-color\n 'horizon-color': '#f8f4f0', // fog-color (or high-color) → horizon-color\n 'fog-color': '#ffffff', // optional, same as high-color\n 'fog-ground-blend': 0.3, // horizon-blend → fog-ground-blend\n 'sky-horizon-blend': 0.3, // optional extra blend control\n 'atmosphere-blend': 1.0 // full atmosphere\n});\n``` | #### Minimal example ```js const map = new maplibregl.Map({ container: 'map', style: 'https://tiles.openfreemap.org/styles/liberty', center: [-122.42, 37.78], zoom: 12, pitch: 45, // needed to see the sky bearing: -17 }); map.on('load', () => { // Turn on the sky (which also gives you fog-like depth) map.setSky({ 'sky-color': '#d8f2ff', 'horizon-color': '#f8f4f0', 'fog-color': '#ffffff', 'fog-ground-blend': 0.3, 'sky-horizon-blend': 0.3, 'atmosphere-blend': 1.0 }); }); ``` **Things to remember** * `sky` is **experimental** in the style spec, but it works in all current MapLibre releases (v5+). * You need a **non-flat pitch** (≥ 30°) to see the sky; otherwise the map looks the same as before. * If you only want a simple fog effect without a sky gradient, you can set `sky-color` to the same value as `horizon-color` and keep the other fog properties. --- ## 3. “Free-camera” APIs → Camera-option helpers ### What you used in Mapbox GL JS v2 ```js const cam = map.getFreeCameraOptions(); // returns {center, zoom, pitch, bearing, altitude, roll} cam.altitude = 2000; map.setFreeCameraOptions(cam); ``` ### MapLibre equivalents MapLibre never exposed a `FreeCameraOptions` class. Instead it provides **utility functions** that calculate a full `CameraOptions` object (center, zoom, pitch, bearing, **elevation**, **roll**) from a geographic position and orientation. You then feed that object to the normal camera methods (`jumpTo`, `easeTo`, `flyTo`). #### Helper 1 – `calculateCameraOptionsFromCameraLngLatAltRotation` ```js // Desired camera position const lngLat = [-122.42, 37.78]; // lon, lat const altitude = 2000; // metres above ground const bearing = -17; // degrees clockwise const pitch = 45; // degrees const roll = 0; // degrees (optional) // Compute the full CameraOptions object const camOpts = map.calculateCameraOptionsFromCameraLngLatAltRotation( lngLat, altitude, bearing, pitch, roll ); // Apply it – you can use jumpTo (instant) or easeTo/flyTo (animated) map.jumpTo(camOpts); // or map.easeTo(camOpts); ``` #### Helper 2 – `calculateCameraOptionsFromTo` (older, still supported) If you want the camera to look **from** one point **to** another (e.g., a “look-at” view), use: ```js const from = [-122.42, 37.78]; const altitudeFrom = 2000; const to = [-122.45, 37.80]; const altitudeTo = 0; // ground level const camOpts = map.calculateCameraOptionsFromTo( from, altitudeFrom, to, altitudeTo ); map.easeTo(camOpts); ``` #### Quick migration cheat-sheet | Mapbox v2 API | MapLibre replacement | |---------------|----------------------| | `map.getFreeCameraOptions()` | *No direct getter* – you can store the last `CameraOptions` you passed to `jumpTo/easeTo/flyTo` or compute a new one with the helpers above. | | `map.setFreeCameraOptions(opts)` | `map.jumpTo(opts)` / `map.easeTo(opts)` / `map.flyTo(opts)` where `opts` is the result of one of the `calculateCameraOptions…` helpers. | | `FreeCameraOptions` type | `CameraOptions` (same shape, but you must compute `elevation`/`roll` yourself). | ### Example: “Fly up 2 km, look down” ```js map.on('load', () => { const target = [-122.42, 37.78]; const altitude = 2000; // metres const cam = map.calculateCameraOptionsFromCameraLngLatAltRotation( target, altitude, 0, // bearing 60, // pitch (steep look-down) 0 // roll ); map.flyTo(cam); }); ``` --- ## 4. Other v2-only features you might have hit | Feature (Mapbox v2) | MapLibre status | How to achieve the same thing | |---------------------|-----------------|------------------------------| | **`map.setTerrain({source: 'terrain-source', exaggeration: 1.5})`** | **Supported** – same API, just make sure the source is a valid DEM (e.g., `maplibre-gl-dem`). | | **`map.setProjection('globe')`** | **Supported** – `map.setProjection({type: 'globe'})` (v5+). | | **`map.addSource('raster', {type: 'raster', url: 'mapbox://...'} )`** | **Not supported** – replace `mapbox://` URLs with HTTP/HTTPS tile URLs (e.g., `https://tiles.openfreemap.org/...`). | | **`mapboxgl.Geocoder`** | Use **`@maplibre/maplibre-gl-geocoder`** (fork) or a third-party geocoder (Nominatim, Peloton, MapTiler). | | **`mapboxgl.NavigationControl`** | Same class name under `maplibregl.NavigationControl`. | | **`mapboxgl.FullscreenControl`** | Same under `maplibregl.FullscreenControl`. | | **`mapboxgl.ScaleControl`** | Same under `maplibregl.ScaleControl`. | | **`mapboxgl.GeolocateControl`** | Same under `maplibregl.GeolocateControl`. | If you see any of the above still failing, double-check that you imported the correct class from `maplibregl` and that the style you are using actually defines the required source/layer. --- ## 5. Full Minimal Working Example (v6 ES-module) ```html MapLibre – fog → sky + free-camera
``` *Run this in a modern browser (Chrome ≥ 106, Edge, Firefox). It demonstrates the two missing pieces working out-of-the-box.* --- ## 6. Debugging Checklist (if something still breaks) | Symptom | Likely cause | Fix | |---------|--------------|-----| | **“Failed to load style”** | Still using a `mapbox://` URL or a style that references Mapbox sprites/glyphs. | Switch to a fully-qualified HTTP style URL, or host your own style JSON and assets. | | **`map.setSky is not a function`** | Using a MapLibre version < v5 (sky was added in v5). | Upgrade to the latest (`npm i maplibre-gl@latest`). | | **`calculateCameraOptionsFromCameraLngLatAltRotation is not a function`** | Same as above – older version. | Upgrade. | | **Controls
